70: func (r *SQLiteRepository) RequestCancellation(ctx context.Context, runID RunID, reason string) (Snapshot, bool, error) {
71: 	if ctx == nil {
72: 		ctx = context.Background()
73: 	}
74: 	if err := runID.Validate(); err != nil {
75: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
76: 	}
77: 	reason = strings.TrimSpace(reason)
78: 	if reason == "" || len(reason) > MaxSafeValueBytes || strings.ContainsAny(reason, "\x00\r\n") {
79: 		return Snapshot{}, false, invalidField("cancellation.reason", "must be a bounded canonical reason")
80: 	}
81: 	now := r.now()
82: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
83: 	if err != nil {
84: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_begin", "begin cancellation request failed", err)
85: 	}
86: 	defer tx.Rollback()
87: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, runID)
88: 	if err != nil {
89: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
90: 	}
91: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.Cancellation.State != CancellationNone {
92: 		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
93: 			return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_read_commit", "finish cancellation state read failed", err)
94: 		}
95: 		return current, false, nil
96: 	}
97: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
98: 	payload, err := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"state": string(CancellationRequested), "reason": reason}, MaxSafeValueBytes*2)
99: 	if err != nil {
100: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
101: 	}
102: 	var attemptValue any
103: 	if current.CurrentAttemptID != "" {
104: 		attemptValue = string(current.CurrentAttemptID)
105: 	}
106: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, attempt_id, payload_json)
107: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'cancellation', ?, ?)`, string(runID), sequence, formatTime(now), attemptValue, payload); err != nil {
108: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_event", "persist cancellation event failed", err)
109: 	}
110: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
111: UPDATE runs SET lifecycle = ?, cancellation_state = ?, cancellation_reason = ?, cancellation_requested_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?
112: WHERE run_id = ? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND cancellation_state = ? AND last_sequence = ?`,
113: 		string(LifecycleCancelling), string(CancellationRequested), reason, formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence,
114: 		string(runID), string(CancellationNone), current.LastSequence)
115: 	if err != nil {
116: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel", "persist cancellation request failed", err)
117: 	}
118: 	if changed, err := result.RowsAffected(); err != nil || changed != 1 {
119: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeConflict, "cancel", runID, "cancellation state changed concurrently", true, err)
120: 	}
121: 	snapshot, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, runID)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
124: 	}
125: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
126: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_commit", "commit cancellation request failed", err)
127: 	}
128: 	r.notify(runID, sequence)
129: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "run cancellation requested",
130: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(runID)}, LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)},
131: 		LogField{Key: "cancellation_state", Value: string(snapshot.Cancellation.State)}, LogField{Key: "cancellation_reason", Value: reason})
132: 	r.metrics.cancellationRequests.Add(1)
133: 	return snapshot, true, nil
134: }

136: func (r *SQLiteRepository) AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx context.Context, fence Fence) (Snapshot, bool, error) {
137: 	if ctx == nil {
138: 		ctx = context.Background()
139: 	}
140: 	if err := fence.Validate(); err != nil {
141: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
142: 	}
143: 	now := r.now()
144: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
145: 	if err != nil {
146: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_begin", "begin cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
147: 	}
148: 	defer tx.Rollback()
149: 	if err := verifyFence(ctx, tx, fence); err != nil {
150: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
151: 	}
152: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, fence.RunID)
153: 	if err != nil {
154: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
155: 	}
156: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.Cancellation.State == CancellationAcknowledged {
157: 		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
158: 			return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_read_commit", "finish cancellation acknowledgement read failed", err)
159: 		}
160: 		return current, false, nil
161: 	}
162: 	if current.Cancellation.State != CancellationRequested {
163: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeConflict, "cancel_ack", fence.RunID, "cancellation has not been requested", false, nil)
164: 	}
165: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
166: 	payload, _ := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"state": string(CancellationAcknowledged)}, MaxSafeValueBytes)
167: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, attempt_id, payload_json)
168: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'cancellation', ?, ?)`, string(fence.RunID), sequence, formatTime(now), string(fence.AttemptID), payload); err != nil {
169: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_event", "persist cancellation acknowledgement event failed", err)
170: 	}
171: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
172: UPDATE runs SET cancellation_state = ?, cancellation_acknowledged_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?
173: WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id = ? AND cancellation_state = ? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND last_sequence = ?`,
174: 		string(CancellationAcknowledged), formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence, string(fence.RunID), string(fence.AttemptID),
175: 		string(CancellationRequested), current.LastSequence)
176: 	if err != nil {
177: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack", "persist cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
178: 	}
179: 	if changed, err := result.RowsAffected(); err != nil || changed != 1 {
180: 		return Snapshot{}, false, runError(CodeStaleFence, "cancel_ack", fence.RunID, "cancellation acknowledgement lost its fence", false, err)
181: 	}
182: 	snapshot, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, fence.RunID)
183: 	if err != nil {
184: 		return Snapshot{}, false, err
185: 	}
186: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
187: 		return Snapshot{}, false, classifyStoreError("cancel_ack_commit", "commit cancellation acknowledgement failed", err)
188: 	}
189: 	r.notify(fence.RunID, sequence)
190: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "run cancellation acknowledged",
191: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(fence.RunID)}, LogField{Key: "attempt_id", Value: string(fence.AttemptID)},
192: 		LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)}, LogField{Key: "cancellation_state", Value: string(snapshot.Cancellation.State)})
193: 	return snapshot, true, nil
194: }

196: func (r *SQLiteRepository) List(ctx context.Context, query Query) (Page, error) {
197: 	limit := query.Limit
198: 	if limit == 0 {
199: 		limit = 50
200: 	}
201: 	if limit < 1 || limit > 200 {
202: 		return Page{}, invalidField("query.limit", "must be between 1 and 200")
203: 	}
204: 	clauses := []string{"1=1"}
205: 	args := make([]any, 0, 8)
206: 	if len(query.Lifecycle) > 0 {
207: 		parts := make([]string, 0, len(query.Lifecycle))
208: 		for _, lifecycle := range query.Lifecycle {
209: 			if !lifecycle.IsValid() {
210: 				return Page{}, invalidField("query.lifecycle", "contains an unknown state")
211: 			}
212: 			parts = append(parts, "?")
213: 			args = append(args, string(lifecycle))
214: 		}
215: 		clauses = append(clauses, "lifecycle IN ("+strings.Join(parts, ",")+")")
216: 	}
217: 	for column, value := range map[string]string{
218: 		"target_kind": query.TargetKind, "project_id": query.Project, "sprint_id": query.Sprint, "study_id": query.Study,
219: 	} {
220: 		if value != "" {
221: 			clauses = append(clauses, column+" = ?")
222: 			args = append(args, value)
223: 		}
224: 	}
225: 	if query.After != "" {
226: 		cursor, err := decodeRunCursor(query.After)
227: 		if err != nil {
228: 			return Page{}, err
229: 		}
230: 		clauses = append(clauses, "(updated_at < ? OR (updated_at = ? AND run_id < ?))")
231: 		args = append(args, cursor.UpdatedAt, cursor.UpdatedAt, string(cursor.RunID))
232: 	}
233: 	rows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `SELECT run_id, updated_at FROM runs WHERE `+strings.Join(clauses, " AND ")+` ORDER BY updated_at DESC, run_id DESC LIMIT ?`, append(args, limit+1)...)
234: 	if err != nil {
235: 		return Page{}, classifyStoreError("list", "list runs failed", err)
236: 	}
237: 	defer rows.Close()
238: 	type listedRun struct {
239: 		id        RunID
240: 		updatedAt string
241: 	}
242: 	listed := make([]listedRun, 0, limit+1)
243: 	for rows.Next() {
244: 		var item listedRun
245: 		if err := rows.Scan(&item.id, &item.updatedAt); err != nil {
246: 			return Page{}, classifyStoreError("list_scan", "decode run list failed", err)
247: 		}
248: 		listed = append(listed, item)
249: 	}
250: 	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
251: 		return Page{}, classifyStoreError("list_rows", "read run list failed", err)
252: 	}
253: 	page := Page{Runs: make([]Snapshot, 0, min(limit, len(listed)))}
254: 	if len(listed) > limit {
255: 		page.NextCursor = encodeRunCursor(runCursor{UpdatedAt: listed[limit-1].updatedAt, RunID: listed[limit-1].id})
256: 		listed = listed[:limit]
257: 	}
258: 	for _, item := range listed {
259: 		snapshot, err := r.Snapshot(ctx, item.id)
260: 		if err != nil {
261: 			return Page{}, err
262: 		}
263: 		page.Runs = append(page.Runs, snapshot)
264: 	}
265: 	return page, nil
266: }

268: type runCursor struct {
269: 	UpdatedAt string `json:"updated_at"`
270: 	RunID     RunID  `json:"run_id"`
271: }
272: 
273: func encodeRunCursor(cursor runCursor) string {
274: 	encoded, _ := json.Marshal(cursor)
275: 	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(encoded)
276: }
277: 
278: func decodeRunCursor(value string) (runCursor, error) {
279: 	encoded, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(value)
280: 	if err != nil || len(encoded) > 1024 {
281: 		return runCursor{}, invalidField("query.after", "is not a valid opaque cursor")
282: 	}
283: 	var cursor runCursor
284: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(encoded, &cursor); err != nil || cursor.UpdatedAt == "" || cursor.RunID.Validate() != nil {
285: 		return runCursor{}, invalidField("query.after", "is not a valid opaque cursor")
286: 	}
287: 	if _, err := parseTime(cursor.UpdatedAt); err != nil {
288: 		return runCursor{}, invalidField("query.after", "is not a valid opaque cursor")
289: 	}
290: 	return cursor, nil
291: }

293: type reconciliationCandidate struct {
294: 	runID      RunID
295: 	attemptID  AttemptID
296: 	ownerID    string
297: 	generation uint64
298: 	process    ProcessIdentity
299: }

301: func (r *SQLiteRepository) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, probe ProcessProbe, opts ReconcileOptions) (ReconcileReport, error) {
302: 	if probe == nil {
303: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("process_probe", "is required")
304: 	}
305: 	grace := opts.Grace
306: 	if grace == 0 {
307: 		grace = ReconciliationGrace
308: 	}
309: 	if grace < 0 {
310: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("reconciliation.grace", "must not be negative")
311: 	}
312: 	limit := opts.Limit
313: 	if limit == 0 {
314: 		limit = DefaultReconcileBatch
315: 	}
316: 	if limit < 1 || limit > MaximumReconcileBatch {
317: 		return ReconcileReport{}, invalidField("reconciliation.limit", fmt.Sprintf("must be between 1 and %d", MaximumReconcileBatch))
318: 	}
319: 	report := ReconcileReport{Decisions: make([]ReconcileDecision, 0, limit)}
320: 	acceptedPredicate, acceptedArgs := r.expiredTimestampPredicate("accepted_at", grace)
321: 	unclaimedRows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
322: SELECT run_id FROM runs
323: WHERE terminal_outcome IS NULL AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND `+acceptedPredicate+`
324: ORDER BY accepted_at ASC, run_id ASC LIMIT ?`, append(acceptedArgs, limit)...)
325: 	if err != nil {
326: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "scan unclaimed runs failed", err)
327: 	}
328: 	var unclaimed []RunID
329: 	for unclaimedRows.Next() {
330: 		var runID RunID
331: 		if err := unclaimedRows.Scan(&runID); err != nil {
332: 			unclaimedRows.Close()
333: 			return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "decode unclaimed run failed", err)
334: 		}
335: 		unclaimed = append(unclaimed, runID)
336: 	}
337: 	if err := unclaimedRows.Close(); err != nil {
338: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "close unclaimed run scan failed", err)
339: 	}
340: 	for _, runID := range unclaimed {
341: 		won, err := r.reconcileUnclaimed(ctx, runID)
342: 		if err != nil {
343: 			return report, err
344: 		}
345: 		if !won {
346: 			continue
347: 		}
348: 		report.Scanned++
349: 		report.Terminal++
350: 		decision := "owner_never_claimed_after_grace"
351: 		candidate := reconciliationCandidate{runID: runID}
352: 		_ = r.recordReconciliation(ctx, candidate, "terminal_proposal", decision)
353: 		report.Decisions = append(report.Decisions, ReconcileDecision{RunID: runID, Action: "terminal_proposal", Decision: decision})
354: 	}
355: 	remaining := limit - report.Scanned
356: 	if remaining == 0 {
357: 		r.finishReconciliationLog(ctx, &report)
358: 		return report, nil
359: 	}
360: 	predicate, predicateArgs := r.expiredLeasePredicate(grace)
361: 	queryArgs := append(predicateArgs, remaining)
362: 	rows, err := r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
363: SELECT runs.run_id, attempts.attempt_id, attempts.owner_id, attempts.fencing_generation,
364:        attempts.host_digest, attempts.boot_id, attempts.pid, attempts.process_birth_token
365: FROM runs JOIN attempts ON attempts.attempt_id = runs.current_attempt_id
366: WHERE runs.terminal_outcome IS NULL AND `+predicate+`
367: ORDER BY attempts.lease_expires_at ASC, runs.run_id ASC LIMIT ?`, queryArgs...)
368: 	if err != nil {
369: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "scan expired run owners failed", err)
370: 	}
371: 	var candidates []reconciliationCandidate
372: 	for rows.Next() {
373: 		var candidate reconciliationCandidate
374: 		if err := rows.Scan(&candidate.runID, &candidate.attemptID, &candidate.ownerID, &candidate.generation,
375: 			&candidate.process.HostDigest, &candidate.process.BootID, &candidate.process.PID, &candidate.process.BirthToken); err != nil {
376: 			rows.Close()
377: 			return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "decode expired run owner failed", err)
378: 		}
379: 		candidates = append(candidates, candidate)
380: 	}
381: 	if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
382: 		return ReconcileReport{}, classifyStoreError("reconcile_scan", "close expired owner scan failed", err)
383: 	}
384: 	report.Scanned += len(candidates)
385: 	for _, candidate := range candidates {
386: 		observed, probeErr := probe.Probe(ctx, candidate.process.PID)
387: 		decision, outcome := reconcileProcessDecision(candidate.process, observed, probeErr)
388: 		action := "terminal_proposal"
389: 		if outcome == "" {
390: 			action = "mark_stalled"
391: 			if err := r.markStalled(ctx, candidate); err != nil {
392: 				if errors.Is(err, ErrTerminal) || errors.Is(err, ErrStaleFence) {
393: 					continue
394: 				}
395: 				return report, err
396: 			}
397: 			report.Stalled++
398: 		} else {
399: 			fence := Fence{RunID: candidate.runID, AttemptID: candidate.attemptID, OwnerID: candidate.ownerID, FencingGeneration: candidate.generation}
400: 			_, won, err := r.ProposeTerminal(ctx, fence, TerminalProposal{Outcome: outcome, Reason: decision, ProposedBy: "reconciler"})
401: 			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ErrTerminal) && !errors.Is(err, ErrStaleFence) {
402: 				return report, err
403: 			}
404: 			if won {
405: 				report.Terminal++
406: 				if outcome == TerminalCleanupUncertain {
407: 					report.Uncertain++
408: 				}
409: 			}
410: 		}
411: 		_ = r.recordReconciliation(ctx, candidate, action, decision)
412: 		report.Decisions = append(report.Decisions, ReconcileDecision{RunID: candidate.runID, AttemptID: candidate.attemptID, Action: action, Decision: decision})
413: 	}
414: 	r.finishReconciliationLog(ctx, &report)
415: 	return report, nil
416: }

418: func (r *SQLiteRepository) finishReconciliationLog(ctx context.Context, report *ReconcileReport) {
419: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "run reconciliation completed",
420: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_scanned", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Scanned)},
421: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_stalled", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Stalled)},
422: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_terminal", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Terminal)},
423: 		LogField{Key: "reconciliation_uncertain", Value: fmt.Sprint(report.Uncertain)})
424: 	r.metrics.reconciliations.Add(1)
425: }

427: func (r *SQLiteRepository) reconcileUnclaimed(ctx context.Context, runID RunID) (wonResult bool, resultErr error) {
428: 	metricStarted := time.Now()
429: 	defer func() { r.metrics.terminal.observe(metricStarted, resultErr) }()
430: 	now := r.now()
431: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
432: 	if err != nil {
433: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_begin", "begin unclaimed reconciliation failed", err)
434: 	}
435: 	defer tx.Rollback()
436: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, runID)
437: 	if err != nil {
438: 		if errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) {
439: 			return false, nil
440: 		}
441: 		return false, err
442: 	}
443: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.CurrentAttemptID != "" {
444: 		return false, nil
445: 	}
446: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
447: 	reason := "owner_never_claimed_after_grace"
448: 	payload, err := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"outcome": string(TerminalInterrupted), "reason": reason}, MaxSafeValueBytes*2)
449: 	if err != nil {
450: 		return false, err
451: 	}
452: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, payload_json)
453: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'terminal', ?)`, string(runID), sequence, formatTime(now), payload); err != nil {
454: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_event", "persist unclaimed terminal event failed", err)
455: 	}
456: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE runs SET lifecycle = ?, liveness = ?, finished_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?,
457: terminal_outcome = ?, terminal_reason = ?, terminal_at = ?, terminal_proposed_by = 'reconciler'
458: WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`,
459: 		string(LifecycleInterrupted), string(LivenessTerminal), formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence,
460: 		string(TerminalInterrupted), reason, formatTime(now), string(runID))
461: 	if err != nil {
462: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "persist unclaimed terminal state failed", err)
463: 	}
464: 	changed, err := result.RowsAffected()
465: 	if err != nil {
466: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "inspect unclaimed terminal state failed", err)
467: 	}
468: 	if changed != 1 {
469: 		return false, nil
470: 	}
471: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
472: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_commit", "commit unclaimed reconciliation failed", err)
473: 	}
474: 	r.notify(runID, sequence)
475: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "unclaimed run reconciled",
476: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(runID)}, LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)},
477: 		LogField{Key: "terminal_outcome", Value: string(TerminalInterrupted)})
478: 	return true, nil
479: }

481: func reconcileProcessDecision(expected, observed ProcessIdentity, probeErr error) (string, TerminalOutcome) {
482: 	if errors.Is(probeErr, ErrProcessNotFound) {
483: 		return "owner_process_missing_after_grace", TerminalInterrupted
484: 	}
485: 	if probeErr != nil {

411: 		_ = r.recordReconciliation(ctx, candidate, action, decision)
412: 		report.Decisions = append(report.Decisions, ReconcileDecision{RunID: candidate.runID, AttemptID: candidate.attemptID, Action: action, Decision: decision})

427: func (r *SQLiteRepository) reconcileUnclaimed(ctx context.Context, runID RunID) (wonResult bool, resultErr error) {
428: 	metricStarted := time.Now()
429: 	defer func() { r.metrics.terminal.observe(metricStarted, resultErr) }()
430: 	now := r.now()
431: 	tx, err := r.db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
432: 	if err != nil {
433: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_begin", "begin unclaimed reconciliation failed", err)
434: 	}
435: 	defer tx.Rollback()
436: 	current, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, tx, runID)
437: 	if err != nil {
438: 		if errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) {
439: 			return false, nil
440: 		}
441: 		return false, err
442: 	}
443: 	if current.Terminal != nil || current.CurrentAttemptID != "" {
444: 		return false, nil
445: 	}
446: 	sequence := current.LastSequence + 1
447: 	reason := "owner_never_claimed_after_grace"
448: 	payload, err := marshalBounded(map[string]string{"outcome": string(TerminalInterrupted), "reason": reason}, MaxSafeValueBytes*2)
449: 	if err != nil {
450: 		return false, err
451: 	}
452: 	if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO events (run_id, sequence, committed_at, event_type, payload_json)
453: VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'terminal', ?)`, string(runID), sequence, formatTime(now), payload); err != nil {
454: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_event", "persist unclaimed terminal event failed", err)
455: 	}
456: 	result, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE runs SET lifecycle = ?, liveness = ?, finished_at = ?, updated_at = ?, last_sequence = ?,
457: terminal_outcome = ?, terminal_reason = ?, terminal_at = ?, terminal_proposed_by = 'reconciler'
458: WHERE run_id = ? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`,
459: 		string(LifecycleInterrupted), string(LivenessTerminal), formatTime(now), formatTime(now), sequence,
460: 		string(TerminalInterrupted), reason, formatTime(now), string(runID))
461: 	if err != nil {
462: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "persist unclaimed terminal state failed", err)
463: 	}
464: 	changed, err := result.RowsAffected()
465: 	if err != nil {
466: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_cas", "inspect unclaimed terminal state failed", err)
467: 	}
468: 	if changed != 1 {
469: 		return false, nil
470: 	}
471: 	if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
472: 		return false, classifyStoreError("reconcile_unclaimed_commit", "commit unclaimed reconciliation failed", err)
473: 	}
474: 	r.notify(runID, sequence)
475: 	r.log(ctx, LogInfo, "unclaimed run reconciled",
476: 		LogField{Key: "run_id", Value: string(runID)}, LogField{Key: "sequence", Value: fmt.Sprint(sequence)},
477: 		LogField{Key: "terminal_outcome", Value: string(TerminalInterrupted)})
478: 	return true, nil
479: }

481: func reconcileProcessDecision(expected, observed ProcessIdentity, probeErr error) (string, TerminalOutcome) {
482: 	if errors.Is(probeErr, ErrProcessNotFound) {
483: 		return "owner_process_missing_after_grace", TerminalInterrupted
484: 	}
485: 	if probeErr != nil {
486: 		return "owner_process_identity_uncertain_after_grace", TerminalCleanupUncertain
487: 	}
488: 	if expected.HostDigest == "" || expected.BootID == "" || expected.BirthToken == "" || observed.HostDigest == "" || observed.BootID == "" || observed.BirthToken == "" {
489: 		return "owner_process_identity_incomplete_after_grace", TerminalCleanupUncertain
490: 	}
491: 	if expected.HostDigest != observed.HostDigest || expected.BootID != observed.BootID || expected.PID != observed.PID || expected.BirthToken != observed.BirthToken {
492: 		return "owner_process_birth_mismatch_after_grace", TerminalInterrupted
493: 	}
494: 	return "exact_owner_process_still_live_but_lease_expired", ""
495: }

522: 		string(candidate.runID), attempt, formatTime(r.now()), action, decision, string(evidence))

535: 	}

538: FROM reconciliation_log ORDER BY observed_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?`, limit)
539: 	if err != nil {
540: 		return nil, classifyStoreError("reconciliation_evidence", "read reconciliation evidence failed", err)
541: 	}
542: 	defer rows.Close()
543: 	result := make([]ReconciliationEvidence, 0, limit)
544: 	for rows.Next() {

548: 		if err := rows.Scan(&item.RunID, &attempt, &observed, &item.Action, &item.Decision, &encodedEvidence); err != nil {

552: 		item.ObservedAt, err = parseTime(observed)
553: 		if err != nil {
554: 			return nil, err
555: 		}
556: 		var stored map[string]string
557: 		if json.Unmarshal([]byte(encodedEvidence), &stored) == nil {
558: 			switch stored["evidence"] {
559: 			case "safe_identity_only", "acceptance_timestamp_only":

566: 		result = append(result, item)

568: 	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
569: 		return nil, classifyStoreError("reconciliation_evidence", "read reconciliation evidence failed", err)
570: 	}

196: 	setPersistenceErr := func(value error) {
197: 		eventMu.Lock()
198: 		defer eventMu.Unlock()
199: 		if persistenceErr == nil {
200: 			persistenceErr = value
201: 			cancel()
202: 		}
203: 	}
204: 	req.OnEvent = func(event runtimepkg.Event) {
205: 		eventMu.Lock()
206: 		defer eventMu.Unlock()
207: 		if persistenceErr != nil {
208: 			return
209: 		}
210: 		draft := runtimeEventDraft(req, event)
211: 		eventAt := event.Time.UTC()
212: 		if eventAt.IsZero() {
213: 			eventAt = time.Now().UTC()
214: 		}
215: 		// Content-aware coalescing: only collapse identical progress payloads within the window.
216: 		// Reasoning/text deltas and tool calls have distinct payload hashes and will not coalesce.
217: 		hash := payloadHash(draft.Payload)
218: 		key := string(draft.Type) + "\x00" + draft.Stage + "\x00" + draft.Task + "\x00" + hash
219: 		elapsed := eventAt.Sub(progressCommittedAt)
220: 		if draft.Type == runcontrol.EventProgress && key == progressKey && elapsed >= 0 && elapsed < runcontrol.ProgressCoalesceWindow {
221: 			if progressOmitted == 0 {
222: 				progressOmittedFirst = eventAt
223: 			}
224: 			progressOmitted++
225: 			progressOmittedLast = eventAt
226: 			return
227: 		}
228: 		if progressOmitted > 0 {
229: 			if draft.Omission == nil {
230: 				draft.Omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced"}
231: 			}
232: 			draft.Omission.Count += progressOmitted
233: 			draft.Omission.FirstAt = &progressOmittedFirst
234: 			draft.Omission.LastAt = &progressOmittedLast
235: 			progressOmitted = 0
236: 		}
237: 		if _, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(runCtx, r.repository, fence, draft); appendErr != nil {
238: 			persistenceErr = fmt.Errorf("persist runtime event: %w", appendErr)
239: 			cancel()
240: 			return
241: 		}
242: 		if draft.Type == runcontrol.EventProgress {
243: 			progressKey = key
244: 			progressCommittedAt = eventAt
245: 		}
246: 		if configuredOnEvent != nil {
247: 			configuredOnEvent(event)
248: 		}
249: 	}
250: 
251: 	controlDone := make(chan struct{})
252: 	go func() {
253: 		defer close(controlDone)
254: 		ticker := time.NewTicker(runcontrol.OwnerTickInterval)
255: 		defer ticker.Stop()
256: 		lastHeartbeat := time.Now()
257: 		lastReconcile := time.Now()
258: 		for {
259: 			select {
260: 			case <-runCtx.Done():
261: 				return
262: 			case now := <-ticker.C:
263: 				snapshot, err := r.repository.Snapshot(runCtx, fence.RunID)
264: 				if err != nil {
265: 					if runCtx.Err() != nil {
266: 						return
267: 					}
268: 					setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("poll durable run control: %w", err))
269: 					return
270: 				}
271: 				if snapshot.Cancellation.State == runcontrol.CancellationRequested {
272: 					if _, _, err := r.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(runCtx, fence); err != nil {
273: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("acknowledge durable cancellation: %w", err))
274: 						return
275: 					}
276: 					cancel()
277: 					return
278: 				}
279: 				if now.Sub(lastHeartbeat) >= runcontrol.HeartbeatInterval {
280: 					if _, err := r.repository.Heartbeat(runCtx, fence, runControlLease); err != nil {
281: 						if runCtx.Err() != nil {
282: 							return
283: 						}
284: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("persist owner heartbeat: %w", err))
285: 						return
286: 					}
287: 					lastHeartbeat = now
288: 				}
289: 				if now.Sub(lastReconcile) >= runcontrol.ReconciliationInterval {
290: 					if _, err := r.repository.Reconcile(runCtx, runcontrol.NativeProcessProbe{}, runcontrol.ReconcileOptions{}); err != nil {
291: 						if runCtx.Err() != nil {
292: 							return
293: 						}
294: 						setPersistenceErr(fmt.Errorf("reconcile durable runs: %w", err))
295: 						return
296: 					}
297: 					lastReconcile = now
298: 				}
299: 			}
300: 		}
301: 	}()
302: 	result, runErr := r.base.StartRun(runCtx, req)
303: 	eventMu.Lock()
304: 	if persistenceErr == nil && progressOmitted > 0 {
305: 		_, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(runCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{
306: 			Type: runcontrol.EventOmission,
307: 			Omission: &runcontrol.Omission{
308: 				Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced", Count: progressOmitted,
309: 				FirstAt: &progressOmittedFirst, LastAt: &progressOmittedLast,
310: 			},
311: 		})
312: 		if appendErr != nil {
313: 			persistenceErr = fmt.Errorf("persist progress omission: %w", appendErr)
314: 		}
315: 	}
316: 	eventMu.Unlock()
317: 	cancel()
318: 	<-controlDone
319: 	eventMu.Lock()
320: 	persistErr := persistenceErr
321: 	eventMu.Unlock()
322: 	if persistErr != nil {
323: 		terminalCtx, terminalCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
324: 		_, _, terminalErr := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{
325: 			Outcome: runcontrol.TerminalPersistenceLost, Reason: "durable event persistence failed", ProposedBy: r.owner.ID,
326: 		})
327: 		terminalCancel()
328: 		if terminalErr != nil {
329: 			return result, errors.Join(persistErr, terminalErr)
330: 		}
331: 		return result, persistErr
332: 	}
333: 
334: 	outcome, reason := terminalOutcome(result, runErr, ctx)
335: 	terminalCtx, terminalCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
336: 	defer terminalCancel()
337: 	if _, _, err := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, r.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{
338: 		Outcome: outcome, Reason: reason, ProposedBy: r.owner.ID,
339: 	}); err != nil {
340: 		return result, errors.Join(runErr, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal run outcome: %w", err))
341: 	}
342: 	return result, runErr
343: }

345: func appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx context.Context, repository runcontrol.Repository, fence runcontrol.Fence, draft runcontrol.EventDraft) (runcontrol.Event, runcontrol.Snapshot, error) {
346: 	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
347: 	for {
348: 		event, snapshot, err := repository.Append(ctx, fence, draft)
349: 		if err == nil || !retryableRunControlError(err) || !time.Now().Before(deadline) {
350: 			return event, snapshot, err
351: 		}
352: 		if err := waitRunControlRetry(ctx, deadline); err != nil {
353: 			return runcontrol.Event{}, runcontrol.Snapshot{}, err
354: 		}
355: 	}
356: }
357: 
358: func proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(ctx context.Context, repository runcontrol.Repository, fence runcontrol.Fence, proposal runcontrol.TerminalProposal) (runcontrol.Snapshot, bool, error) {
359: 	for {
360: 		snapshot, won, err := repository.ProposeTerminal(ctx, fence, proposal)
361: 		if err == nil || !retryableRunControlError(err) {
362: 			return snapshot, won, err
363: 		}
364: 		if err := waitRunControlRetry(ctx, time.Now().Add(250*time.Millisecond)); err != nil {
365: 			return runcontrol.Snapshot{}, false, err
366: 		}
367: 	}
368: }
369: 
370: func retryableRunControlError(err error) bool {
371: 	return errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrUnavailable) || errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrBusy)
372: }
373: 
374: func waitRunControlRetry(ctx context.Context, deadline time.Time) error {
375: 	wait := time.Until(deadline)
376: 	if wait > 100*time.Millisecond {
377: 		wait = 100 * time.Millisecond
378: 	}
379: 	if wait <= 0 {
380: 		return context.DeadlineExceeded
381: 	}
382: 	timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
383: 	defer timer.Stop()
384: 	select {
385: 	case <-ctx.Done():
386: 		return ctx.Err()
387: 	case <-timer.C:
388: 		return nil
389: 	}
390: }

392: func targetFromRuntimeRequest(req runtimepkg.Request) runcontrol.Target {
393: 	target := runcontrol.Target{
394: 		Kind:      boundedSafe(req.PromptRef.OwnerKind),
395: 		Operation: boundedSafe(req.PromptRef.Purpose),
396: 		Project:   boundedSafe(req.Metadata["project"]),
397: 		Sprint:    boundedSafe(req.Metadata["sprint"]),
398: 		Study:     boundedSafe(req.Metadata["study"]),
399: 		Stage:     boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]),
400: 		Task:      boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"], req.Metadata["coverage"])),
401: 	}
402: 	if target.Kind == "" {
403: 		if target.Study != "" {
404: 			target.Kind = "study"
405: 		} else if target.Sprint != "" {
406: 			target.Kind = "sprint"
407: 		} else {
408: 			target.Kind = "runtime"
409: 		}
410: 	}
411: 	if target.Operation == "" {
412: 		target.Operation = boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(target.Stage, req.Metadata["task.kind"], req.PromptRef.ID, "runtime"))
413: 	}
414: 	return target
415: }

417: func runtimeEventDraft(req runtimepkg.Request, event runtimepkg.Event) runcontrol.EventDraft {
418: 	eventType := runcontrol.EventProgress
419: 	lowerType := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Type))
420: 	lowerKind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(event.Kind))
421: 	switch lowerType {
422: 	case "warning", "warn", "error":
423: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
424: 	case "artifact", "file":
425: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventArtifact
426: 	case "finding":
427: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventFinding
428: 	case "message", "text", "output", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text", "reasoning", "content", "delta":
429: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
430: 	default:
431: 		// Kind-based fallback: reasoning and message kinds should be visible as message, not coalesced progress.
432: 		switch lowerKind {
433: 		case "message", "reasoning", "assistant", "assistant_text", "reasoning_text":
434: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventMessage
435: 		case "tool", "tool_use", "tool_call", "tool_call_update":
436: 			// Tools stay as progress but with distinct payload so coalescing can distinguish.
437: 			eventType = runcontrol.EventProgress
438: 		}
439: 	}
440: 	payload := map[string]string{
441: 		"runtime_event_id": boundedSafe(event.ID),
442: 		"runtime_run_id":   boundedSafe(event.RunID),
443: 		"session_id":       boundedSafe(event.SessionID),
444: 		"type":             boundedSafe(event.Type),
445: 		"kind":             boundedSafe(event.Kind),
446: 	}
447: 	if lowerKind == "tool" || lowerKind == "tool_use" || lowerKind == "tool_call" || lowerKind == "tool_call_update" {
448: 		captureToolObservation(payload, event.Payload)
449: 	}
450: 	// Preserve safe observable payload fields into durable storage for observability.
451: 	// Deny sensitive keys and truncate values to runcontrol-safe limits.
452: 	// Flatten one level of nesting so tool/action names buried in maps are surfaced as top-level payload keys
453: 	// that the run timeline JS expects (payload.tool, payload.action, payload.title, etc.).
454: 	for key, value := range event.Payload {
455: 		if isSensitivePayloadKey(key) {
456: 			continue
457: 		}
458: 		normalized := strings.TrimSpace(key)
459: 		if normalized == "" || len(normalized) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(normalized, "\x00\r\n") {
460: 			continue
461: 		}
462: 		if normalized == "type" || normalized == "kind" {
463: 			continue
464: 		}
465: 		if nested, ok := value.(map[string]any); ok {
466: 			for subKey, subVal := range nested {
467: 				if isSensitivePayloadKey(subKey) {
468: 					continue
469: 				}
470: 				subNorm := strings.TrimSpace(subKey)
471: 				if subNorm == "" || len(subNorm) > 128 || strings.ContainsAny(subNorm, "\x00\r\n") {
472: 					continue
473: 				}
474: 				if _, exists := payload[subNorm]; exists {
475: 					continue
476: 				}
477: 				// Promote common observable sub-keys; namespace the rest to avoid collisions.
478: 				promote := map[string]bool{"tool": true, "title": true, "detail": true, "text": true, "delta": true, "content": true, "message": true, "action": true, "state": true, "status": true, "native_type": true, "line": true}
479: 				targetKey := subNorm
480: 				if !promote[subNorm] {
481: 					targetKey = normalized + "_" + subNorm
482: 					if len(targetKey) > 128 {
483: 						continue
484: 					}
485: 				}
486: 				if _, exists := payload[targetKey]; exists {
487: 					continue
488: 				}
489: 				str := payloadValueString(subVal)
490: 				if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
491: 					continue
492: 				}
493: 				if len(payload) >= 30 {
494: 					break
495: 				}
496: 				payload[targetKey] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
497: 			}
498: 			// Also keep a compact stringified top-level for debugging if not promoted.
499: 			if len(payload) < 30 {
500: 				if _, exists := payload[normalized]; !exists {
501: 					str := payloadValueString(value)
502: 					if strings.TrimSpace(str) != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(str, "[map omitted") {
503: 						payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
504: 					}
505: 				}
506: 			}
507: 			continue
508: 		}
509: 		str := payloadValueString(value)
510: 		if strings.TrimSpace(str) == "" {
511: 			continue
512: 		}
513: 		if len(payload) >= 30 {
514: 			break
515: 		}
516: 		if _, exists := payload[normalized]; exists {
517: 			continue
518: 		}
519: 		payload[normalized] = boundedPayloadValue(str)
520: 	}
521: 	// Ensure the most useful display keys are always present even if nested.
522: 	for _, want := range []string{"tool", "action", "title", "detail", "text", "delta"} {
523: 		if _, ok := payload[want]; ok {
524: 			continue
525: 		}
526: 		if v := findNestedString(event.Payload, want); v != "" {
527: 			payload[want] = boundedPayloadValue(v)
528: 		}
529: 	}
530: 	omission := (*runcontrol.Omission)(nil)
531: 	if event.RawPresent || event.RawOmitted {
532: 		reason := firstSafeValue(event.RawOmissionReason, "runtime payload omitted by safe persistence policy")
533: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe(reason), Count: 1}
534: 	} else if len(event.Payload) > len(payload)-5 {
535: 		// Payload had more fields than we persisted (truncated/omitted keys) – record for diagnostics but don't hide persisted fields.
536: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: boundedSafe("runtime payload truncated to safe observable fields"), Count: 1}
537: 	}
538: 	return runcontrol.EventDraft{
539: 		Type: eventType, Scope: runcontrol.EventScopeRuntime,
540: 		Stage: boundedSafe(req.Metadata["stage"]), Task: boundedSafe(firstSafeValue(req.Metadata["task"], req.Metadata["task.kind"])),
541: 		Kind: payload["kind"], Tool: payload["tool"], Action: payload["action"],
542: 		Reason: payload["reason"], Detail: firstSafeValue(payload["detail"], payload["title"]),
543: 		Payload: payload, Omission: omission,
544: 	}
545: }

547: func isSensitivePayloadKey(key string) bool {
548: 	lower := strings.ToLower(key)
549: 	for _, marker := range []string{"secret", "token", "password", "authorization", "cookie", "api_key", "apikey", "credential", "auth"} {
550: 		if strings.Contains(lower, marker) {
551: 			return true
552: 		}
553: 	}
554: 	return false
555: }

557: func findNestedString(payload map[string]any, want string) string {
558: 	for _, v := range payload {
559: 		if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
560: 			if s, ok := m[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
561: 				return s
562: 			}
563: 			// One more level deep (common for opencode part.state structures)
564: 			for _, inner := range m {
565: 				if innerMap, ok := inner.(map[string]any); ok {
566: 					if s, ok := innerMap[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
567: 						return s
568: 					}
569: 				}
570: 			}
571: 		}
572: 	}
573: 	return ""
574: }

576: func payloadValueString(value any) string {
577: 	switch v := value.(type) {
578: 	case string:
579: 		return v
580: 	case []byte:
581: 		if len(v) == 0 {
582: 			return ""
583: 		}
584: 		return string(v)
585: 	case bool:
586: 		if v {
587: 			return "true"
588: 		}
589: 		return "false"
590: 	case int:
591: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
592: 	case int8:
593: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
594: 	case int16:
595: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
596: 	case int32:
597: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
598: 	case int64:
599: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
600: 	case uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64:
601: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", v)
602: 	case float32, float64:
603: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
604: 	case map[string]any, map[string]string, []any, []string:
605: 		// Encode structured values compactly.
606: 		encoded, err := jsonMarshalTruncated(v)
607: 		if err != nil {
608: 			return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
609: 		}
610: 		return encoded
611: 	default:
612: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)
613: 	}
614: }
615: 
616: func jsonMarshalTruncated(v any) (string, error) {
617: 	encoded, err := json.Marshal(v)
618: 	if err != nil {
619: 		return "", err
620: 	}
621: 	return string(encoded), nil
622: }

624: func captureToolObservation(out map[string]string, payload map[string]any) {
625: 	for target, aliases := range map[string][]string{
626: 		"tool_call_id": {"tool_call_id", "toolCallId", "call_id", "callID"},
627: 		"tool_name":    {"tool_name", "toolName", "tool", "name"},
628: 		"tool_status":  {"tool_status", "status", "phase"},
629: 	} {
630: 		if value := findNestedPayloadValue(payload, aliases, 0); value != nil {
631: 			if text, ok := value.(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(text) != "" {
632: 				out[target] = boundedPayloadValue(text)
633: 			}
634: 		}
635: 	}
636: 	for target, aliases := range map[string][]string{
637: 		"tool_arguments": {"tool_arguments", "arguments", "args", "input", "parameters"},
638: 		"tool_result":    {"tool_result", "result", "output", "content"},
639: 		"tool_error":     {"tool_error", "error"},
640: 	} {
641: 		value := findNestedPayloadValue(payload, aliases, 0)
642: 		if value == nil {
643: 			continue
644: 		}
645: 		encoded, err := json.Marshal(redactObservableValue(value))
646: 		if err == nil && string(encoded) != "null" {
647: 			out[target] = boundedPayloadValue(string(encoded))
648: 		}
649: 	}
650: 	if out["tool"] == "" {
651: 		out["tool"] = out["tool_name"]
652: 	}
653: }
654: 
655: func findNestedPayloadValue(value any, aliases []string, depth int) any {
656: 	if depth > 5 {
657: 		return nil
658: 	}
659: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
660: 	case map[string]any:
661: 		for _, key := range aliases {
662: 			if found, ok := typed[key]; ok && found != nil {
663: 				return found
664: 			}
665: 		}
666: 		keys := make([]string, 0, len(typed))
667: 		for key := range typed {
668: 			keys = append(keys, key)
669: 		}
670: 		sort.Strings(keys)
671: 		for _, key := range keys {
672: 			if found := findNestedPayloadValue(typed[key], aliases, depth+1); found != nil {
673: 				return found
674: 			}
675: 		}
676: 	case []any:
677: 		for _, item := range typed {
678: 			if found := findNestedPayloadValue(item, aliases, depth+1); found != nil {
679: 				return found
680: 			}
681: 		}
682: 	}
683: 	return nil
684: }
685: 
686: func redactObservableValue(value any) any {
687: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
688: 	case map[string]any:
689: 		redacted := make(map[string]any, len(typed))
690: 		for key, item := range typed {
691: 			if isSensitivePayloadKey(key) {
692: 				redacted[key] = "[REDACTED]"
693: 			} else {
694: 				redacted[key] = redactObservableValue(item)
695: 			}
696: 		}
697: 		return redacted
698: 	case []any:
699: 		redacted := make([]any, len(typed))
700: 		for index, item := range typed {
701: 			redacted[index] = redactObservableValue(item)
702: 		}
703: 		return redacted
704: 	case string:
705: 		lower := strings.ToLower(typed)
706: 		for _, marker := range []string{"bearer ", "sk-", "ghp_", "github_pat_", "-----begin private key"} {
707: 			if strings.Contains(lower, marker) {
708: 				return "[REDACTED]"
709: 			}
710: 		}
711: 		return typed
712: 	default:
713: 		return value
714: 	}
715: }
716: 
717: func boundedPayloadValue(value string) string {
718: 	value = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
719: 		if r == 0 || r == '\r' || r == '\n' {
720: 			return -1
721: 		}
722: 		return r
723: 	}, strings.TrimSpace(value))
724: 	if len(value) > runcontrol.MaxSafeValueBytes {
725: 		value = value[:runcontrol.MaxSafeValueBytes]
726: 	}
727: 	return value
728: }
729: 
730: func payloadHash(payload map[string]string) string {
731: 	if len(payload) == 0 {
732: 		return ""
733: 	}
734: 	// Stable hash of payload content for coalescing: include type/kind and any payload_* keys.
735: 	keys := make([]string, 0, len(payload))
736: 	for k := range payload {
737: 		if k == "runtime_event_id" || k == "runtime_run_id" || k == "session_id" {
738: 			continue
739: 		}
740: 		keys = append(keys, k)
741: 	}
742: 	// Keep deterministic order by sorting.
743: 	sortStrings(keys)
744: 	var b strings.Builder
745: 	for _, k := range keys {
746: 		b.WriteString(k)
747: 		b.WriteString("=")
748: 		b.WriteString(payload[k])
749: 		b.WriteString("\x00")
750: 	}
751: 	return b.String()
752: }
753: 
754: func sortStrings(values []string) {
755: 	// Insertion sort for small slices – avoid importing sort for minimal diff; keep stdlib sort if available.
756: 	for i := 1; i < len(values); i++ {
757: 		j := i

Required tests include ordered-stage transitions, old flow-state compatibility, path/range validation, source-read/output-write isolation, fake runtime output, missing/invalid output, atomic rerun, model/variant fallback, CLI/JSON/TUI/web parity, exact prefix equality across representative downstream stages, absence of dynamic prefix data, flow execution exactly once, cancellation, and recovery.

The web extensibility gate requires the new stage to expose status, artifact preview, operation start, progress, cancellation, findings, and recovery through the existing application capability model. Adding route-specific product logic for `code-context` fails the gate.

## 18C. Phase 6 Durable Run Control And Observation

The current in-memory operation hub is a compatibility/delivery mechanism, not an adequate execution control plane. Sprint 35 must provide one workspace-wide model shared by CLI, TUI, browser pages, and every local server instance within the explicitly supported topology.

The durable run envelope must include, directly or through stable references:

```text
workspace-scoped run ID
operation kind and project/study/sprint/stage target
accepted / queued / running / terminal lifecycle timestamps
attempt, stage, task, agentwrap run/session, process, and external-harness correlations
owner identity, renewable lease, heartbeat, fencing value, and safe process-birth identity
latest durable event sequence and retention boundary
cancellation request/acknowledgement facts
one immutable arbitrated terminal result or explicit cleanup uncertainty
safe diagnostics, schema version, and migration metadata
```

Acceptance of a runtime-backed execution is atomic with durable run creation and happens before child execution. If required acceptance persistence fails, the child does not start. Event records are redacted before persistence, assigned monotonically increasing per-run sequences, and committed before live fan-out. The store may compact detail, but it must retain an explicit snapshot and lower replay boundary so clients can distinguish complete replay from a gap.

Active-run queries are workspace-wide. Product-page status may filter the common projection, but the global running count cannot be derived from the current page, browser session, or one server's memory. Planning stage readiness and operational execution lifecycle are separate types; UI code must not infer `running` from a stage-status enum that cannot represent it.

Read visibility is independent from originating-session continuity. Mutation still requires fresh authorization and a resolvable current owner. Cancellation is idempotent, durably recorded, routed through the canonical product/runtime cancellation path, and arbitrated against completion, failure, timeout, interruption, shutdown, and reconciliation so only one terminal outcome wins.

Liveness is conservative. A PID alone is insufficient because of PID reuse. Lease expiry, missing process, missing owner, artifact presence, or lost server memory cannot independently prove completion. Reconciliation uses fencing or equivalent stale-writer protection, records its evidence and decisions, and exposes `stalled`, `interrupted`, or `cleanup_uncertain` where truth cannot be proven.

The following are required reasoning decisions, not preselected implementation requirements:

- same-host multi-process versus shared-filesystem multi-host support and the guarantees at that boundary
- dedicated coordinator/daemon, fenced direct repository writers, or a hybrid
- filesystem snapshot/journal, SQLite, agentwrap store composition, or another smallest sufficient durable mechanism
- interface/package ownership without moving workflow semantics out of study/sprint modules or duplicating agentwrap
- worker cancellation versus safe adoption after owner loss
- run/attempt/stage/task identity hierarchy and correlation format
- lease duration, heartbeat cadence, clock assumptions, fencing, and process-birth verification
- replay guarantee, deduplication, cursor expiry, retention, compaction, snapshot, backpressure, and disk-limit policy
- cross-session read policy versus cancel/retry authorization
- compatibility and tombstone behavior for legacy operation URLs, locks, state files, and checkpoints
- local metrics/health interfaces, optional trace export, and support-bundle scope
- safe behavior when acceptance, mid-run append, heartbeat, or terminal persistence fails

Every chosen mechanism must pass the same cross-process failure matrix: two CLI runs visible globally; a second supported server replaying and then following a current run; browser-session expiry; observer restart; abrupt owner death; stale lease and PID reuse; duplicate cancellation; completion/cancellation races; slow subscribers; cursor expiry; corrupt/torn records; disk-full or permission failure; bounded retention; and redaction. Tests must prove that operational records never override canonical product artifacts or stage verdicts.

## 18D. Gated Post-Phase-6 Technical Direction

The following sequence is directional and does not authorize implementation until a later sprint selects it explicitly:

1. **Content identity/provenance pilot:** optional versioned YAML frontmatter with minimal `schema`, `id`, `type`, `title`, `status`, and `authority`; selective semantic block IDs; revision-aware evidence; warning-first validation; legacy files remain valid.
2. **Read-only QA:** retain `review` compatibility while presenting it as Conformance Review; introduce a separate `VerificationPhase`; map changed behavior into deterministic bounded shards; allow read-only investigation and synthesis only.
3. **Evidence QA and repair:** require isolated writable investigation workspaces before generated tests/probes; adjudicate evidence globally before issue promotion; permit production repair only from frozen evidence-backed issue packets; bound cycles and expose stalled/escalated outcomes.
4. **Derived retrieval:** build deterministic semantic records and a measured lexical baseline first. Indexes are disposable, preserve exact authoritative text/provenance/status, and never override project/sprint context selection. Embeddings remain deferred until lexical evaluation proves a gap.
5. **Product persistence/SQLite:** first classify authored artifacts, checkpoints, derived data, operational state, run evidence, and repository source. Sprint 35 operational run storage does not select a new authored-artifact authority. Extract focused package-owned repositories only for proven workflows; keep Git/source and execution workspaces filesystem-native; select one product-artifact authority at composition; prohibit generic virtual filesystems, silent dual writes, and premature sync.
6. **Knowledge graph:** only after stable explicit relationships and retrieval baseline demonstrate multi-hop need, build a deterministic in-memory read-only projection. - Text and JSON output.

- Level.
- Command.
- Workspace.
- Study.
- Project.
- Sprint.
- Run ID.
- Run schema version.
- Owner and fencing identity when applicable.
- Task ID.
- Stage/execution ID.
- Attempt.
- Runtime.
- Model.
- Event type.
- Message.
- Agentwrap run ID.
- Agentwrap session ID.
- Agentwrap event kind.
- Agentwrap policy decision when applicable.

### 19.2 Diagnostics

Diagnostics must include:

- Runtime executable path.
- Runtime version when available.
- Working directory.
- Timeout.
- Exit code.
- Safe stderr excerpt.
- Validation failures.
- State file path.

- Durable run record path/store identity and schema version.

- Current lifecycle snapshot, last event sequence, oldest retained sequence, and any replay gap.

- Cancellation request, routing, acknowledgement, and cleanup certainty.

Diagnostics must not include:

- API keys.
- Full sensitive environment.
- Secret config values.

### 20.1 Concurrency

- Use `context.Context` for cancellation.
- Use bounded goroutine pools for tasks.
- Avoid unbounded channels.
- Drain `agentwrap.Run.Events()` or deliberately discard through a draining goroutine until the channel closes.
- Ensure `agentwrap.Run.Wait()` is called for every started run.
- Let the agentwrap adapter own subprocess waiting and cleanup.
- Ensure no goroutine leaks in tests.
- Bound HTTP request concurrency, active operations, SSE subscribers, and per-operation event buffers.
- Never let an SSE write or slow browser subscriber block the underlying app operation.
- Serialize or fence competing lifecycle writers so stale owners cannot renew leases, append authoritative transitions, or overwrite the winning terminal outcome.
- Bound durable journal queues, append latency, retained bytes/events, replay work, reconciliation concurrency, and support-bundle size.

### 20.2 Cancellation

Cancellation sources:

- User interrupt.
- Context cancellation.
- Timeout.
- Runtime failure.

Cancellation behavior:

- Stop scheduling new tasks.
- Cancel active task contexts and call `agentwrap.Run.Cancel`.
- Let the agentwrap adapter attempt runtime process termination and cleanup.
- Save state.
- Mark active tasks cancelled or retryable based on policy.
- Return cancellation exit code when user initiated.
- Preserve agentwrap cleanup metadata separately from the primary run result.
- Disconnecting an SSE subscriber cancels only that subscription; explicit operation cancellation uses the operation context and shared app cancellation path.
- Graceful server shutdown stops accepting new work, closes subscribers, cancels workers owned by that server under the selected topology, and leaves durable product and operational state recoverable.

- Cancellation from another supported process is first persisted against the run, then routed to the current fenced owner. Repetition is safe and an unreachable owner remains visibly pending or uncertain until reconciliation.

Reconciliation uses fencing or equivalent stale-writer protection, records its evidence and decisions, and exposes `stalled`, `interrupted`, or `cleanup_uncertain` where truth cannot be proven.

The following are required reasoning decisions, not preselected implementation requirements:

- same-host multi-process versus shared-filesystem multi-host support and the guarantees at that boundary
- dedicated coordinator/daemon, fenced direct repository writers, or a hybrid
- filesystem snapshot/journal, SQLite, agentwrap store composition, or another smallest sufficient durable mechanism
- interface/package ownership without moving workflow semantics out of study/sprint modules or duplicating agentwrap
- worker cancellation versus safe adoption after owner loss
- run/attempt/stage/task identity hierarchy and correlation format
- lease duration, heartbeat cadence, clock assumptions, fencing, and process-birth verification
- replay guarantee, deduplication, cursor expiry, retention, compaction, snapshot, backpressure, and disk-limit policy
- cross-session read policy versus cancel/retry authorization
- compatibility and tombstone behavior for legacy operation URLs, locks, state files, and checkpoints
- local metrics/health interfaces, optional trace export, and support-bundle scope
- safe behavior when acceptance, mid-run append, heartbeat, or terminal persistence fails

Every chosen mechanism must pass the same cross-process failure matrix: two CLI runs visible globally; a second supported server replaying and then following a current run; browser-session expiry; observer restart; abrupt owner death; stale lease and PID reuse; duplicate cancellation; completion/cancellation races; slow subscribers; cursor expiry; corrupt/torn records; disk-full or permission failure; bounded retention; and redaction. Tests must prove that operational records never override canonical product artifacts or stage verdicts.

## 18D. Gated Post-Phase-6 Technical Direction

The following sequence is directional and does not authorize implementation until a later sprint selects it explicitly:

1. **Content identity/provenance pilot:** optional versioned YAML frontmatter with minimal `schema`, `id`, `type`, `title`, `status`, and `authority`; selective semantic block IDs; revision-aware evidence; warning-first validation; legacy files remain valid.
2. **Read-only QA:** retain `review` compatibility while presenting it as Conformance Review; introduce a separate `VerificationPhase`; map changed behavior into deterministic bounded shards; allow read-only investigation and synthesis only.
3. **Evidence QA and repair:** require isolated writable investigation workspaces before generated tests/probes; adjudicate evidence globally before issue promotion; permit production repair only from frozen evidence-backed issue packets; bound cycles and expose stalled/escalated outcomes.
4. **Derived retrieval:** build deterministic semantic records and a measured lexical baseline first. Indexes are disposable, preserve exact authoritative text/provenance/status, and never override project/sprint context selection. Embeddings remain deferred until lexical evaluation proves a gap.
5. **Product persistence/SQLite:** first classify authored artifacts, checkpoints, derived data, operational state, run evidence, and repository source. Sprint 35 operational run storage does not select a new authored-artifact authority. Extract focused package-owned repositories only for proven workflows; keep Git/source and execution workspaces filesystem-native; select one product-artifact authority at composition; prohibit generic virtual filesystems, silent dual writes, and premature sync.
6. **Knowledge graph:** only after stable explicit relationships and retrieval baseline demonstrate multi-hop need, build a deterministic in-memory read-only projection. Keep edge provenance/origin, status, revision, contradiction, and supersession explicit. A persistent graph remains derived and rebuildable; a graph database is not assumed.
7. **Authority/cloud/Aren:** compare filesystem, SQLite/server, and hybrid publication modes on real work before choosing. Cloud and typed Aren artifact tools reuse proven application contracts; source edits/builds/tests remain sandboxed filesystem/Git work.

Every branch must stop when its evidence gate fails. In particular: no repair without adjudicated evidence and isolation; no retrieval before content dogfood; no SQLite merely for architectural cleanliness; no graph persistence before useful bounded traversal; no cloud authority before local authority and recovery semantics are proven.

## 19. Logging and Diagnostics

UltraPlan logging and diagnostics must consume agentwrap observability records rather than directly inspecting native runtime process streams.

### 19.1 Logger Requirements

- Context-aware logging.
- Text and JSON output.
- Log levels: debug, info, warn, error.
- Redaction support.
- Stable fields for structured logs.

Structured log fields:

- Timestamp.
- Level.
- Command.
- Workspace.
- Study.
- Project.
- Sprint.
- Run ID.
- Run schema version.
- Owner and fencing identity when applicable.
- Task ID.
- Stage/execution ID.
- Attempt.
- Runtime.
- Model.
- Event type.
- Message.
- Agentwrap run ID.
- Agentwrap session ID.
- Agentwrap event kind.
- Agentwrap policy decision when applicable.
- Durable event sequence and replay boundary when applicable.
- Lifecycle transition, lease state, reconciliation decision, and terminal-outcome winner when applicable.

### 19.2 Diagnostics

Diagnostics must include:

- Runtime executable path.
- Runtime version when available.
- Working directory.
- Timeout.
- Exit code.
- Safe stderr excerpt.
- Validation failures.
- State file path.
- Agentwrap `RunMetadata` summaries for attempts, policy, validation, repair, sessions, permissions, cleanup, artifacts, usage, warnings, and errors.
- Agentwrap raw payload omission/safety facts when relevant.
- Durable run record path/store identity and schema version.
- Owner, lease, heartbeat age, fencing, and safe process-birth facts.
- Current lifecycle snapshot, last event sequence, oldest retained sequence, and any replay gap.
- Acceptance/append/terminal persistence health, reconciliation backlog, and last decision evidence.
- Cancellation request, routing, acknowledgement, and cleanup certainty.

Diagnostics must not include:

- API keys.
- Full sensitive environment.
- Secret config values.

### 19.3 Agentwrap Stores and Sinks

UltraPlan must use agentwrap observability hooks:

- `agentwrap.ObservingRuntime` for active/completed run projections.
- `agentwrap.EventSink` for event fan-out to logs and local event records.
- `agentwrap.RunStore` for run inspection.

`agentwrap.MemoryRunStore` is suitable for isolated tests only. Sprint 35 production paths require an UltraPlan durable operational store correlated with agentwrap records. The selected storage mechanism is a reasoning output; filesystem files are not mandated if they cannot satisfy the required atomicity, concurrency, replay, and recovery contracts.

Required sink failures must be treated according to agentwrap semantics: returned from `Wait` when the primary runtime outcome succeeded. Best-effort sink failures must be recorded as warnings without replacing the primary outcome.

## 20. Concurrency and Cancellation

### 20.1 Concurrency

- Use `context.Context` for cancellation.
- Use bounded goroutine pools for tasks.
- Avoid unbounded channels.
- Drain `agentwrap.Run.Events()` or deliberately discard through a draining goroutine until the channel closes.
- Ensure `agentwrap.Run.Wait()` is called for every started run.
- Let the agentwrap adapter own subprocess waiting and cleanup.
- Ensure no goroutine leaks in tests.
- Bound HTTP request concurrency, active operations, SSE subscribers, and per-operation event buffers.
- Never let an SSE write or slow browser subscriber block the underlying app operation.
- Serialize or fence competing lifecycle writers so stale owners cannot renew leases, append authoritative transitions, or overwrite the winning terminal outcome.
- Bound durable journal queues, append latency, retained bytes/events, replay work, reconciliation concurrency, and support-bundle size.

### 20.2 Cancellation

Cancellation sources:

- User interrupt.
- Context cancellation.
- Timeout.
- Runtime failure.

Cancellation behavior:

- Stop scheduling new tasks.
- Cancel active task contexts and call `agentwrap.Run.Cancel`.
- Let the agentwrap adapter attempt runtime process termination and cleanup.
- Save state.
- Mark active tasks cancelled or retryable based on policy.
- Return cancellation exit code when user initiated.
- Preserve agentwrap cleanup metadata separately from the primary run result.
- Disconnecting an SSE subscriber cancels only that subscription; explicit operation cancellation uses the operation context and shared app cancellation path.
- Graceful server shutdown stops accepting new work, closes subscribers, cancels workers owned by that server under the selected topology, and leaves durable product and operational state recoverable.
- Shutdown cancellation records `reason: server_shutdown`, is idempotent, and participates in the same single-terminal-outcome arbitration as user cancellation, failure, timeout, and completion.
- The server waits only for a configured bounded cleanup period, does not release locks before ownership is reconciled, and records `interrupted` or `cleanup_uncertain` when complete cleanup cannot be proven.
- Forced termination is reconciled at startup; stale `running` state, missing processes, or partial artifacts never imply successful completion.
- Cancellation from another supported process is first persisted against the run, then routed to the current fenced owner. Repetition is safe and an unreachable owner remains visibly pending or uncertain until reconciliation.

# Context Pack: `run-journal-fencing` — Run-control SQLite journal and fencing

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen; working tree differs only in internal/sprint smoke files, runcontrol+app identical).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: durability-core. Risk: critical. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

`internal/runcontrol` is the durable identity and arbitration layer for every executing UltraPlan operation (doc.go:1-6). It records: the accepted execution (`runs`), at most one fenced owner attempt per run (`attempts`), a strictly ordered append-only sanitized event journal (`events`), optional operation alias identities for dedup (`operation_aliases`), and reconciliation decision evidence (`reconciliation_log`) — all in one private SQLite database at `.ultraplan/run-control.db`. It deliberately does NOT own product workflow state, artifacts, or runtime supervision (doc.go, interfaces.go:47-48). Core mechanisms: accept-before-execute; fenced claim with lease + heartbeat; cancellation request/acknowledge split across processes; single-winner terminal compare-and-set over seven outcomes including explicit uncertainty (`cleanup_uncertain`, `persistence_degraded`); conservative birth-identity reconciliation that never infers success.

## 2. Entrypoints and control flow

### 2.1 Open path (`sqlite.go:60-134`)
`OpenSQLite(ctx, workspaceRoot, SQLiteOptions)`: validate workspace root (abs, dir, sqlite.go:136-152) → prepare private storage (`preparePrivateDatabase`, :154-191): `.ultraplan/` created 0700, symlink/non-dir rejected via Lstat (:159-165); `run-control.db` created `O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_RDWR` 0600, symlink/non-regular rejected (:172-186); `enforcePrivateMode` chmods then re-stats to verify exact mode (:193-205) → open DSN with fixed pragmas `_busy_timeout=5000 _foreign_keys=on _journal_mode=WAL _synchronous=FULL _txlock=immediate _defensive=1` (:73-80) → ping, then `verifyPragmas` reads back journal_mode/synchronous/foreign_keys/busy_timeout only (:207-227) → `migrateSchema` (migration.go:25-82; current-version DBs take the lock-free verify path — schema record equality + integrity check; migration itself belongs to surface `run-recovery-retention`) → connection pool default 4, operator-cappable 1..16 (:92-100) → repository assembled with injected-or-wall Clock, RandomIDSource, normalized retention policy (:107-131).

### 2.2 Accept (`sqlite.go:378-470`)
Quota gates first: `storageBytes()` sums sizes of all regular files whose names start with `run-control.db` in `.ultraplan/` (retention.go:35-56 — includes `-wal`/`-shm`/`.migrate.lock`/backups); usage ≥ 80% of hard quota triggers inline `Compact(ctx,64)` (:384-390); usage ≥ soft quota (hard − 16 MiB headroom) refuses acceptance with retryable `CodeQuota` (:391-395). Then Target/Correlation validation, ProductStatus/ConfirmationDigest ≤ MaxSafeValueBytes (:396-404), RunID minted when absent and validated (:405-415), correlation marshaled bounded to 256 KiB (:416). One immediate transaction inserts the `runs` row (lifecycle `accepted`, liveness `unknown`, record_state `full`, cancellation_state `none`, last_sequence 0) (:429-444); duplicate RunID → typed Conflict (:440-442). Optional OperationAlias inserts an `operation_aliases` row in the same tx; alias conflict → Conflict (:445-455). Snapshot loaded + validated inside the tx before commit (:456-462). NOTE: Accept writes NO event row; the journal stays empty until the first cancellation/append/terminal/reconcile write.

### 2.3 Claim (`sqlite.go:486-592`)
Validates RunID/Owner/Correlation/Lease>0 and AttemptID (minted when absent) (:490-512). In one immediate transaction: read lifecycle+current_attempt (:529); terminal run → `CodeTerminal`; existing current attempt → `CodeConflict` "run already has a current owner attempt" (:533-538). Next lifecycle = running, preserved as cancelling if already cancelling (:539-542). Ordinal = MAX(ordinal)+1 and fencing_generation = MAX(fencing_generation)+1 over the run's attempts (:543-546); attempts table enforces `UNIQUE(run_id,ordinal)` and `UNIQUE(run_id,fencing_generation)` (:288-289) plus `fencing_generation > 0` (:278). INSERT attempt (owner_id, host_digest, boot_id, pid, process_birth_token, claimed_at=heartbeat_at=now, lease_expires_at=now+lease) (:547-560), then CAS-style UPDATE of runs: `SET current_attempt_id=?, lifecycle=?, liveness='live', started_at=COALESCE(started_at,?), updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → Conflict (:561-571). Snapshot validated pre-commit. Because no code path ever nulls `current_attempt_id`, each run is claimed AT MOST once in its lifetime (grep over package: only setter is sqlite.go:563; reconcile paths require it NULL/non-terminal).

## 5. Invariants (as implemented)

- Identity grammar: RunID/AttemptID are `run_`/`att_` + 26 lowercase canonical base32 chars = exactly 128 bits (id.go:73-89); validated at every entry point; generated via crypto/rand.
- Single owner per run lifetime: claim requires `current_attempt_id IS NULL`; nothing ever clears it; late claims hit CodeConflict (live) or CodeTerminal (terminal).
- Fencing: every mutation by an owner goes through verifyFence (attempt row + owner + generation + runs.current_attempt_id agreement) plus per-statement CAS guards (last_sequence for Append/Ack/Cancel; terminal_outcome IS NULL everywhere; outcome IS NULL on heartbeat attempts-row update). Stale writers get typed CodeStaleFence, never silent success.
- Monotonic journal: sequences allocated as MAX+1 inside immediate transactions; immutability trigger blocks UPDATE; compaction only DELETEs non-authoritative types (progress/message/omission; tombstone adds accepted/claimed/lifecycle/recovery) and advances oldest_retained_sequence + history_complete=0 so readers can detect gaps.
- Single-winner terminal: one CAS-guarded transition; later proposers receive (incumbent, won=false); append-after-terminal CodeTerminal; request-cancellation-after-terminal idempotent no-op returning the winner; completion may win AFTER requested cancellation (test-pinned) leaving cancellation_state='requested' frozen beside a succeeded terminal.
- Active-state machine: validActiveTransition grammar; 'cancelling' absorbing among active states; terminal reachable only through the two arbitration paths.
- Cancellation request/acknowledge split: request is ownerless and idempotent; acknowledge is fenced; states none→requested→acknowledged ('uncertain' reserved/unwritten).
- Conservative liveness: stall (exact live identity + expired lease) never terminalizes; interrupted requires missing process or exact birth mismatch; anything unprovable → cleanup_uncertain; success is NEVER inferred by reconciliation.
- Quota/liveness coupling: soft gate pauses new accepts (retryable), hard gate blocks non-reserved appends and heartbeats while always permitting reserved recovery types (lifecycle/warning/cancellation/recovery/terminal/omission).
- Boundedness: target fields 512 B; safe values 32 KiB; correlations ≤256 KiB encoded; payloads ≤256 KiB; whole sanitized draft ≤128 KiB else replaced by a warning stub carrying omission metadata; per-run journal ≤4096 events/16 MiB; reconciliation evidence ≤16 KiB; log line ≤4 KiB/file ≤1 MiB; support export ≤1 MiB.
- Durability posture: WAL + synchronous FULL + immediate transactions on every mutation; busy_timeout 5 s; four pragmas verified at open; chmod-verified 0700/0600 private modes; symlink/non-regular rejection at directory, database, and log layers.
- Time authority: production expiry math executes inside SQLite so all processes share the database clock; injected clocks swap to parameter comparison (tests only — no production injector exists, map-02 X6).
- Typed error taxonomy with Retryable flags; SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED→busy(retryable), PERM/READONLY→permission, CORRUPT/NOTADB→corrupt, FULL→quota(retryable), constraint(19)→typed conflicts; context errors pass through unwrapped (errors.go, classifyStoreError sqlite.go:1088-1111).

## 6. Trust boundaries

- Durable rows re-read as input: snapshots/events/evidence decode persisted JSON and timestamps strictly (malformed → CodeCorrupt surfaced to callers, sqlite.go:840,846,965); structural legality enforced by schema CHECKs plus post-load Snapshot.Validate. Anyone able to write the db file can rewrite gate inputs; controls are filesystem privacy (0700/0600, symlink rejection) + validation, not cryptographic integrity.
- Agent-derived event payloads pass TWO gates before storage: producer-side filtering in app (`runtimeEventDraft` run_control.go:417-545 — sensitive-key denylist secret/token/password/authorization/cookie/api_key/apikey/credential/auth, bounded values, one-level flattening, tool observation redaction replacing secret-shaped strings) and the storage-side sanitizer (`sanitizeEventDraft` sanitize.go:26-61 — allowlist of ~40 product field names, sensitive-fragment denylist secret/token/credential/password/prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command, absolute/drive-letter paths and bearer/sk-/ghp_/github_pat_/private-key markers rejected, NUL/CR/LF stripped, oversize drafts replaced wholesale by a warning stub). Dropped detail becomes Omission counts, never silence.
- Structured logs apply the same sanitizer families locally (local_log.go:69-97: sensitive keys dropped, unsafe values "[omitted]", bounds enforced).
- Reconciliation evidence is deliberately reduced at WRITE time to a class string; the reader re-allowlists to two known values with "omitted" fallback (lifecycle.go:556-565).
- Pagination cursors are opaque bounded base64 JSON with canonical-ID and timestamp revalidation (lifecycle.go:278-291).
- Process identity from /proc or sysctl is treated as exact-birth proof only when complete; partial data classifies uncertain rather than dead (interfaces.go:17-20 contract comment).
- The local workspace is the trust domain: any local process with filesystem access to `.ultraplan/` can accept/claim/cancel/terminalize runs; there is no additional authorization layer between `run cancel` and the database.

## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics

Effects confined to the workspace `.ultraplan/` tree and its own projections: row inserts/updates/deletes in one SQLite db (WAL sidecars), chmod enforcement, append-only log, migration lock file (other surface), best-effort wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)+incremental_vacuum after Compact (retention.go:151-152). No network, no signals to foreign processes (probes are read-only), no notifier wired.

Cancellation semantics: user/browser/TUI cancel persists `requested` (idempotent; changed=false on repeats or post-terminal); each owner control loop observes it within ≤1 tick, acknowledges (fenced), then cancels its own context; work drains through product-owned paths; terminal arbitration afterwards decides cancelled-vs-completed with single-winner guarantee. Shutdown: server drain writes leaseless cleanup-uncertain markers elsewhere; runcontrol terminals ride detached 30 s contexts so shutdown cannot prevent terminal commit (shutdown-ordering-chain seam).

Restart/crash semantics: abrupt owner death leaves running rows with expiring leases; startup Reconcile (every process open) plus periodic reconciles convert them to interrupted/cleanup_uncertain using birth-identity proof; unclaimed stale acceptances become interrupted after 45 s grace; repeated reconciliation is idempotent (process_integration_test.go:229-232). Restarted work is a NEW run (claim-once rule), correlated via Correlation.ProductRunID/ParentRun context, never adopted.

Retry/error semantics: busy/unavailable classified retryable; app spine retries appends ≤5 s and terminal proposals indefinitely-with-yields; quota failures stop acceptance/appends but reserve recovery-type writes; permission loss and closed pools produce typed failures with verified no-state-change (fault_test.go:87-129); SQLITE_FULL mid-append leaves last committed sequence intact (fault_test.go:12-50). Observation failures never mutate durable state (follow returns nil on ctx.Done; SSE handlers just stop streaming).

## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence)

From ultraplan-workspace projects/ultraplan-go/docs/TRD.md §18C Phase 6 (~L2185-2212): durable envelope MUST include workspace-scoped run ID, target correlation, lifecycle timestamps, attempt/agentwrap/process correlations, owner identity + renewable lease + heartbeat + fencing value + safe process-birth identity, latest sequence + retention boundary, cancellation request/acknowledgement facts, ONE immutable arbitrated terminal result or explicit cleanup uncertainty. Acceptance atomic with run creation BEFORE child execution; persistence failure ⇒ child does not start. Events redacted before persistence, monotonic per-run sequences, committed before live fan-out; compaction must retain snapshot + lower replay boundary. Liveness conservative: "A PID alone is insufficient because of PID reuse"; reconciliation uses fencing or equivalent, records evidence and decisions, exposes stalled/interrupted/cleanup_uncertain where truth cannot be proven. Read visibility independent of originating session; cancellation idempotent, durably recorded, arbitrated so only one terminal wins.
TRD §20.1 (~L2330): serialize or fence competing lifecycle writers so stale owners cannot renew leases, append authoritative transitions, or overwrite the winning terminal outcome. TRD §20.2 (~L2356): cancellation from another supported process is FIRST persisted against the run, THEN routed to the current fenced owner; repetition safe; unreachable owner remains visibly pending/uncertain until reconciliation. §19.1/19.2: structured log/diagnostic fields include owner/fencing identity, lease state, reconciliation decisions, replay boundary; diagnostics must not include API keys/secrets. Sprint 35 requirements (workspace sprints/35-durable-run-observability/requirements.md L24, L40-41): startup and periodic reconciliation never infer success from process absence or artifact presence; exactly one terminal outcome wins across all races; repeated observers/cancellations cannot rewrite it. HISTORY note: TRD lists topology choices (coordinator vs fenced direct writers) as reasoning outputs; shipped choice is fenced direct multi-process repository access (sqlite.go:41-42 comment).
